title: Uncovering novel functions of NUF2 in glioblastoma and MRI-based expression prediction.
authors: Zhong, Rong-de; Liu, Yun-Sheng; Li, Qian; Kou, Zeng-Wei; Chen, Fan-Fan; Wang, Heng; Zhang, Na; Tang, Han; Zhang, Yuan; Huang, Guo-Dong
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦胶质母细胞瘤中NUF2的致癌功能及MRI影像组学表达预测，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a lethal brain tumor with limited therapies. NUF2, a kinetochore protein involved in cell cycle regulation, shows oncogenic potential in various cancers; however, its role in GBM pathogenesis remains unclear. In this study, we investigated NUF2's function and mechanisms in GBM and developed an MRI-based machine learning model to predict its expression non-invasively, and evaluated its potential as a therapeutic target and prognostic biomarker. Functional assays (proliferation, colony formation, migration, and invasion) and cell cycle analysis were conducted using NUF2-knockdown U87/U251 cells. Western blotting was performed to assess the expression levels of beta-catenin and MMP-9. Bioinformatic analyses included pathway enrichment, immune infiltration, and single-cell subtype characterization. Using preoperative T1CE Magnetic Resonance Imaging sequences from 61 patients, we extracted 1037 radiomic features and developed a predictive model using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression for feature selection and random forest algorithms for classification with rigorous cross-validation. NUF2 overexpression in GBM tissues and cells was correlated with poor survival (p < 0.01). Knockdown of NUF2 significantly suppressed malignant phenotypes (p < 0.05), induced G0/G1 arrest (p < 0.01), and increased sensitivity to TMZ treatment via the beta-catenin/MMP9 pathway. The radiomic model achieved superior NUF2 prediction (AUC = 0.897) using six optimized features. Key features demonstrated associations with MGMT methylation and 1p/19q co-deletion, serving as independent prognostic markers. NUF2 drives GBM progression through beta-catenin/MMP9 activation, establishing its dual role as a therapeutic target and a prognostic biomarker. The developed radiogenomic model enables precise non-invasive NUF2 evaluation, thereby advancing personalized GBM management. This study highlights the translational value of integrating molecular biology with artificial intelligence in neuro-oncology.
abstract_zh: 多形性胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）是一种致死性脑肿瘤，治疗手段有限。NUF2作为一种参与细胞周期调控的动粒蛋白，在多种癌症中显示出致癌潜力；然而，其在GBM发病机制中的作用仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们探讨了NUF2在GBM中的功能与机制，开发了一种基于MRI的机器学习模型以无创预测其表达，并评估了其作为治疗靶点和预后生物标志物的潜力。使用NUF2敲低的U87/U251细胞进行了功能实验（增殖、集落形成、迁移和侵袭）及细胞周期分析。采用Western blotting评估beta-catenin和MMP-9的表达水平。生物信息学分析包括通路富集、免疫浸润和单细胞亚型表征。利用61例患者的术前T1CE磁共振成像序列，我们提取了1037个影像组学特征，并使用最小绝对收缩和选择算子回归进行特征选择及随机森林算法进行分类，同时进行了严格的交叉验证，开发了预测模型。NUF2在GBM组织和细胞中的过表达与不良生存相关（p < 0.01）。敲低NUF2显著抑制恶性表型（p < 0.05），诱导G0/G1期阻滞（p < 0.01），并通过beta-catenin/MMP9通路增加对TMZ治疗的敏感性。影像组学模型使用六个优化特征实现了优异的NUF2预测性能（AUC = 0.897）。关键特征显示出与MGMT甲基化和1p/19q联合缺失的关联，可作为独立的预后标志物。NUF2通过beta-catenin/MMP9激活驱动GBM进展，确立了其作为治疗靶点和预后生物标志物的双重作用。所开发的影像基因组学模型能够实现精确的无创NUF2评估，从而推进GBM的个体化管理。本研究强调了在神经肿瘤学中将分子生物学与人工智能相结合转化应用的价值。
